claim: The group's Capacity Reservation preference decides how reserved capacity is used: with capacity-reservations-only, instances fail to launch when no reserved capacity is available; with capacity-reservations-first, they launch as On-Demand instead.
question: What happens when no reserved capacity is left under the capacity-reservations-only and capacity-reservations-first preferences?

evidence.quote: The Capacity Reservation preference (`CapacityReservationPreference`) tells Auto Scaling how to consume Capacity Reservations when launching instances.
If no reserved capacity is available, instances fail to launch.
If no reserved capacity is available, instances launch as On-Demand.

note: Demand d56. The value names (capacity-reservations-only, capacity-reservations-first, default, none) are on the page as code labels before each sentence.

claim: An Auto Scaling group can launch into reserved capacity: a Capacity Reservation reserves EC2 capacity in a specific Availability Zone so it is there when the group needs to launch, and a Capacity Block expires with Amazon EC2 terminating the instances running in it.
question: Why would an Auto Scaling group target Capacity Reservations, and what happens when a Capacity Block expires?

values.display: reserves Amazon EC2 compute capacity in a specific Availability Zone
Amazon EC2 terminates the instances running in it

evidence.quote: A Capacity Reservation reserves Amazon EC2 compute capacity in a specific Availability Zone, so that capacity is available when your Auto Scaling group needs to launch instances.
When the Capacity Block expires, Amazon EC2 terminates the instances running in it.
